page: Microsoft Azure FX48-24ms_v2 is a constrained-core, high-frequency instance configured for workloads requiring massive memory footprints coupled with high per-core compute performance. Running on Microsoft Hyper-V, the virtual machine provides 24 dedicated vCPUs derived from 12 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor. The CPU features a 4.2 GHz clock speed, a generous 260 MB L3 cache, and integrated hardware acceleration support including AVX-512 and Intel AMX tile and int8 execution units. No local storage is bundled with the instance, requiring attached remote network storage volumes for persistence, and it operates without discrete GPU accelerators.

The instance delivers an atypical resource density by pairing 24 vCPUs with 1008.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 42 GB of RAM per vCPU. This configuration is reflected in its performance metrics, demonstrating top-tier single-core compute performance with a Geekbench single-core score of 2356.0 and strong uncached large-block memory write bandwidth reaching 120.35 GB/sec. Text processing and lightweight LLM text generation also score in the top tier, while multi-core compute tests such as stress-ng and software compilation align within the median band due to the constrained physical core count.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the FX48-24ms_v2 is optimized to minimize per-core software licensing expenses. Workloads bound by database or analytics licensing models benefit from the high 4.2 GHz clock speed and large memory buffer without paying for idle or surplus CPU execution threads. The trade-off involves lower overall aggregate multi-threaded throughput compared to full-core variants and complete reliance on remote storage latency.

This hardware configuration is specifically suited for in-memory databases, electronic design automation (EDA), financial modeling, large-scale graph analytics, and licensed relational database engines that require substantial memory capacity per licensed core.
description: Microsoft Azure FX48-24ms_v2 is a memory-dense, compute-focused virtual machine designed to maximize per-core capacity while reducing core-based software licensing costs. Driven by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz, the instance delivers 24 dedicated vCPUs across 12 physical cores with 260 MB of L3 cache, accompanied by 1008.0 GB of system memory. It includes no local storage or discrete GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Benchmark testing demonstrates exceptional single-core processing capabilities, placing in the top tier on Geekbench single-core and text processing metrics, alongside strong large-block memory write bandwidth of 120.35 GB/sec. The instance trades aggregate parallel throughput for high per-thread performance and extreme memory density, making it a targeted solution for memory-intensive enterprise databases, in-memory caching systems, financial risk simulations, and electronic design automation workloads.
